name: Nexus Integration Data-Carry Ring
description:
A plain titanium ring with an embedded encrypted data storage core capable of holding 2TB of information. Data is transferred via skin-contact NFC when the wearer touches a compatible terminal. The ring has no external indicators — no lights, no markings, no visible technology. It looks like an ordinary band.

The preferred dead-drop medium for information brokers and corporate espionage operatives. A handshake can transfer gigabytes. A ring left on a bar counter can contain enough proprietary data to collapse a corponation's stock price.
functionality: 2TB encrypted storage, contact-transfer data exchange, zero visual indicators
what_it_says: You carry secrets that could ruin lives, and they fit on one finger.
story_hooks: A Data-Carry Ring found on a corpse contains 2TB of encrypted data that no one can crack — three different factions are now willing to kill for a ring that might contain nothing of value.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively simple titanium band that appears entirely unremarkable — the kind of ring anyone might wear. Its minimalist design creates an impression of understated elegance or practical simplicity, depending on context. On the hand, it catches light with a subtle metallic sheen but draws no attention. Perfect anonymity.
physical_description.fit: Snug but not constrictive; sized to sit flush against the skin for optimal NFC contact. Worn on any finger, though index or middle finger is standard for data transfer operatives.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium alloy with embedded encrypted data core (composition proprietary to Nexus Integration). Non-reactive, biocompatible.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, polished finish with barely perceptible micro-ridging from manufacturing. Cool to the touch. No seams, no visible joints — seamlessly integrated.
physical_description.color_scheme: Brushed titanium gray with subtle warm undertones. No accent colors, no markings, no serial numbers visible to the naked eye.
physical_description.closures: None — a continuous band, permanently sealed. The data core is inaccessible without corporate-level decryption hardware.
distinctive_features: Zero external indicators (no LEDs, no haptic feedback, no visible tech)
Imperceptible weight difference from standard titanium rings
NFC activation requires skin contact with compatible terminal
Military-grade encryption that survives biometric scanning
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 corporate espionage asset or Tier 3 information broker tool — the cost is accessible to mid-level operatives, but its utility marks the wearer as plugged into high-value networks.
physical_description.cultural_context: Information broker, corporate intelligence operative, black-market fixer, or someone deep in the shadow economy. Wearing this signals you deal in data as currency. It's the ring of someone whose handshake might be worth Φ500,000 to the right buyer.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always pristine — scratches or damage compromise the NFC field. Obsessively maintained. A worn ring is a dead ring.
